The `using` keyword declares a resource that is disposed automatically when the scope exits, even on throw or early return: it calls the object's [Symbol.dispose]() method, and `await using` calls [Symbol.asyncDispose]() for async cleanup. Multiple resources are disposed in reverse order of declaration. It needs TS 5.2 with the esnext.disposable lib, and the runtime must provide Symbol.dispose or be polyfilled. Action: no code changes; if you want to use it in the repo I'll check our tsconfig target and lib settings and the Node version we run first.

structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays, undefined values and circular references, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, Maps and Sets into empty objects, drops undefined and functions, and throws on cycles. structuredClone throws a DataCloneError on functions and DOM nodes, and neither one preserves class prototypes. So the reviewer is usually right to flag the JSON trick, unless a JSON-safe copy is deliberately wanted. Action: no code change; if you paste the PR line I'll say which case it falls under.

They're not the same: keep-alive only reuses the TCP connection, but on it requests still go one at a time, so a slow response blocks the ones behind it, which is why browsers open several connections per host. HTTP/2 multiplexing interleaves many request and response streams on a single connection at once, with header compression, so no extra connections are needed. HTTP/2 still has head-of-line blocking at the TCP level on packet loss, which HTTP/3 over QUIC addresses. Action: nothing to change in the repo; I can write a two-line version for standup if you want.

tsx uses esbuild to strip the types and run the file, so it starts almost instantly and handles ESM, CommonJS and tsconfig paths without setup, but it does not type-check. ts-node uses the real TypeScript compiler and catches type errors as it runs, but it's slower to start and ESM needs a loader flag. So use tsx for scripts, and keep tsc --noEmit in CI for type checking. Action: nothing to change; the lockfile still needs an install after the package.json edit.
